title: Laboratory spiking process of soil with various uranium and other heavy metals
author: Chen, Larson, et al.

steps.title: Air‑dry soil
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the characterized soil until all moisture is removed, selecting soil that meets the study requirements.

steps.title: Grind and sieve soil
steps.instruction: Grind the dried soil with a wood plate and grinding rod, then pass the ground material through a 2 mm sieve.

steps.title: Calculate metal loading mass
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amount of metal species (UO₃ and uranyl nitrate hexahydrate) based on the desired loading level and the total weight of soil to be spiked.

steps.title: Grind metal compounds to powder
steps.instruction: Using an agate mortar, completely grind the metal compounds (solid UO₃ and uranyl nitrate hexahydrate) into a fine powder.

steps.title: Grind soil to fine powder
steps.instruction: Grind approximately 25–50 g of soil in an agate mortar to a fine powder; the mass should be roughly 10–20 times the mass of the metal salts.

steps.title: Combine metal and soil powders
steps.instruction: Mix the ground metal powder with the fine‑ground soil in the mortar using grinding rods until the mixture is uniformly combined.

steps.title: Homogenize mixture on plastic sheet
steps.instruction: Place the mixture at the centre of a clean 2 m × 2 m plastic sheet, flip the sheet corners diagonally toward the centre 5–8 times, then add bulk clean soil in increments of about 10–20 times the current mixture mass, each time repeating the diagonal‑flipping 5–8 times, until all clean soil is incorporated and the mixture is fully homogenized.

substeps.instruction: Place mixture on 2 m × 2 m plastic sheet
Add bulk soil (≈10–20 × mixture) and repeat flipping 5–8 times until complete

steps.title: Bag, invert, and subsample mixture
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenized soil into a clean plastic bag, continuously invert the bag and repeat 5–8 times, then divide the treated soil evenly into separate containers to obtain the desired number of representative subsamples for experimental replicates.

steps.title: Apply safety and decontamination procedures
steps.instruction: Perform all steps inside a laboratory hood while wearing dust masks, double gloves, Tyvek suits, and rad‑detector/survey tools. Discard contaminated sheets, gloves, masks, and suits in a designated radioactive waste container, and survey all personnel with a rad meter before leaving the hood.

steps.title: Weigh subsample for digestion
steps.instruction: Weigh exactly 1.0 g of each homogenized soil subsample into a digestion tube; prepare duplicates in 50 mL tubes.

steps.title: Acid digestion of soil
steps.instruction: Add 25 mL of 4 M HNO₃ to each tube and place the tubes in a water bath at 80 °C for 16 h to digest the soil.

steps.title: Filter digested solution
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant from each tube and filter it through a 0.45 µm membrane filter.

steps.title: Dilute filtrate for analysis
steps.instruction: Dilute the filtered digest to the appropriate volume with deionised water for ICP‑MS measurement.

steps.title: Measure metals by ICP‑MS
steps.instruction: Analyze the diluted solutions for uranium and other heavy metals using ICP‑MS.
